# Design patterns — what to build once you are connected

> **July 2026 snapshot.** Where this file says "UI-only", "no REST verb" or "walled", read it as a dated verdict:
> many were overturned later (KB `lessons/overturned-beliefs.md`, Laws 16-19). Before telling a user
> something is not possible, work the workaround ladder in KB `knowledge/00-start-here/08 New Pipeline Milestones`.
> "Org A" / "Org B" are two example orgs; derive your own values (Law 1).

Everything else in this corpus answers 'will the platform let me?'. This section answers 'what should I build?' — the mapping shapes, expression idioms, orchestration and quality patterns an IDMC pipeline is actually made of.

⚠️ **EVIDENCE CLASS: third-party reference implementation, NOT live-probed and NOT vendor doctrine.** Distilled from a banking-deposits pipeline design (CDC → SCD Type 2 → star schema, CDI + CDQ + CDGC over a storage-only warehouse). The expression syntax and pattern shapes are standard Informatica and transfer directly; the architectural opinions are one team's defensible choices, not rules. Treat every row as a starting template to validate, never as proven behaviour.

Why it belongs here: mapping and taskflow authoring is a UI-only wall, so none of this is headless-executable. It is guidance for what to build in the canvas — which is exactly the question that follows 'the connection works'.

## Expression idioms — the language is NOT SQL

| Need | Informatica expression | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Conditional / NVL | IIF(ISNULL(CDC_OPERATION), 'INSERT', CDC_OPERATION) | IIF is the ternary. There is no CASE WHEN. ISNULL() tests null, and empty-string is NOT null — test both when a field is 'required'. |
| Current timestamp | SYSTIMESTAMP() | Not NOW(), not CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. Stamp every landed row with it plus the run id. |
| Concatenate | FIRST_NAME \|\| ' ' \|\| LAST_NAME | Pipe-pipe, as in SQL. Beware: concatenating a NULL yields NULL — wrap volatile fields in IIF/ISNULL first. |
| Change-detection hash | MD5(SEGMENT \|\| KYC_STATUS \|\| EMAIL \|\| ADDRESS \|\| CITY \|\| STATE) | The backbone of SCD2 and of 'did anything actually change'. Fix the field ORDER and never reorder it — a reorder invalidates every stored hash and reprocesses the whole dimension. |
| Date arithmetic | DATEADD(DAY, -1, $$LOAD_DATE) | Used to expire an SCD2 row the day before the new version starts. |
| Build a date surrogate key | TO_NUMBER(TO_CHAR(TRANSACTION_DATE,'YYYYMMDD')) | The conventional DIM_DATE join key. Two nested conversions, not a cast. |
| Runtime parameter | $$LOAD_DATE, $$PIPELINE_RUN_ID, $$SOURCE_DIR | Double-dollar is a parameter resolved from a CDI parameter set at runtime. Single-dollar is a system variable. Never hardcode a date, path or connection name. |

## Transformation naming — a convention worth adopting verbatim

| Prefix | Transformation | Why the convention pays |
|---|---|---|
| EXP_ | Expression — derive fields, stamp metadata, build reject reasons | A mapping canvas is read visually. A consistent prefix makes the data flow legible at a glance and makes a spec reviewable without opening the tool — which matters because there is no REST API to diff a mapping. |
| LKP_ | Lookup — resolve a surrogate key, fetch the current dimension row, dedup check | Also signals a performance hotspot: every LKP_ is a round trip. |
| FIL_ | Filter — drop rows that must not proceed | Pair every FIL_ with a reject path or you are silently dropping data. |
| RTR_ | Router — split one stream into named groups (e.g. NEW vs CHANGED) | Prefer a Router over two Filters when the groups are mutually exclusive: one pass, and the intent is explicit. |
| MT_ / M_ / TF_ | Mapping task / mapping / taskflow | M_ is the design asset, MT_ the runnable task wrapping it, TF_ the orchestration. Keep them 1:1 and same-named — `POST /api/v2/mttask` only wraps an existing mapping (`APP_13533` if you forget). |

## SCD Type 2 — the canonical recipe

| Step | Implementation | Trap |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Read the increment | Source the RAW table filtered to `PIPELINE_RUN_ID = $$PIPELINE_RUN_ID` | Filter by run id, not by date: a re-run of the same business date must be idempotent. |
| 2. Look up the current row | LKP on the dimension WHERE `IS_CURRENT = TRUE`, return the surrogate key, stored hash and effective-start date | Looking up without the IS_CURRENT predicate returns every historical version and multiplies rows. |
| 3. Compute the new hash | EXP: `NEW_HASH = MD5(<business attributes, fixed order>)` | Hash only the attributes whose change should create a new version. Including a load timestamp makes every row change every run. |
| 4. Keep only real changes | FIL: `ISNULL(LKP_SK) OR NEW_HASH != LKP_RECORD_HASH` | This single condition is what separates SCD2 from a re-load. Without it the dimension grows every run with identical versions. |
| 5. Split new vs changed | RTR groups — NEW: `ISNULL(LKP_SK)` · CHANGED: `NOT ISNULL(LKP_SK) AND NEW_HASH != LKP_RECORD_HASH` | Two different target behaviours, so route rather than branch downstream. |
| 6. Expire the old version | Target A, load type UPDATE, key `SK = LKP_SK`: set `EFF_END_DATE = DATEADD(DAY,-1,$$LOAD_DATE)`, `IS_CURRENT = FALSE` | Expire-then-insert against the SAME table. Ordering matters: a failure between the two leaves two current rows, so make the task atomic and abort on error. |
| 7. Insert the new version | Target B, load type INSERT: `EFF_START_DATE = $$LOAD_DATE`, `EFF_END_DATE = NULL`, `IS_CURRENT = TRUE`, `RECORD_HASH = NEW_HASH`, surrogate key from a CDI sequence | Carry the run id onto the row (`CREATED_BY_PIPELINE`) — without it you cannot answer 'which run produced this'. |

## Quality and reject handling — never drop a row silently

| Pattern | Implementation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Structured reject sink | Every failed row goes to an ERROR table carrying: run id, source entity, business key, reject reason (rule id + code + the offending value), and the FULL raw record as JSON/VARIANT | Storing the raw record is what makes reprocessing possible. A reject table without it is a count, not a remediation path. |
| Reject reason format | `CQ-002 \| INVALID_EMAIL_FORMAT \| EMAIL='x@invaliddomain'` | Rule id + code + value. A bare 'validation failed' costs a human an hour per incident. |
| Reject-rate circuit breaker | If the reject rate exceeds a threshold (e.g. >10%), FAIL the quality task and abort the taskflow | Per-row rejects are normal; a mass reject means the source contract changed. Loading 90% of a feed and calling it success is the failure mode this prevents. |
| Rule types available | Null check · pattern match (regex) · reference-table domain (IN-list) · date range | Domain checks belong in a reference table, not a hardcoded IN-list, so the domain is reusable and visible to stewards. |
| Fail vs flag | Choose per rule: Reject (row does not proceed) or Flag/warn (row proceeds, marked) | Not every violation is fatal. An unexpected CDC operation code may warrant a warning; a null business key never does. |
| Deduplication | LKP against the fact table on the natural key, then FIL `ISNULL(LKP_SK)` | Makes a re-run safe. Without it, re-processing a file doubles the facts. |

## Layering and orchestration

| Element | Pattern | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Layers | RAW (append-only, immutable audit of every ingest) → CURATED (modelled, mutable) → ERROR (rejects) | RAW being append-only is what lets you reprocess without re-fetching the source, and gives an auditor a defensible answer about what arrived. |
| Stamp on landing | Every RAW row gets run id, source file name, load timestamp | Three columns that make every later question answerable. Add them in the ingest mapping, not afterwards. |
| Taskflow shape | Master TF → child TFs: INGEST → QUALITY → CURATED, with CURATED sequential so FK dependencies hold (dimension before fact) | Parallelism inside a stage is fine; across stages it corrupts referential integrity. |
| Error policy | RAW ingest failure → abort all. Quality breach → abort. Curated failure → abort (never a partial dimension). Per-row reject within threshold → route and continue | State the policy per scenario up front. The default of 'keep going' is what produces half-loaded dimensions nobody notices for a week. |
| Parameterization | One taskflow + a parameter set; the scheduler passes `$$LOAD_DATE` and filenames/connections resolve from it | One definition serves every run — no code change between environments or dates. This is the difference between a demo and something operable. |
| Push-down vs in-tool | Decide deliberately whether transformation logic lives in IDMC or in the warehouse | The source design puts ALL logic in IDMC (warehouse = storage only) so rules are reusable, visible in lineage, and editable by non-SQL users. That is a legitimate stance with a real cost (less push-down performance) — not an Informatica requirement. Choose consciously and write the choice down. |

## How to use this section

These are templates to adapt, not rows to quote as platform behaviour. When a customer or engineer asks 'how would I build X in IDMC', start from the matching pattern, then validate the specific expressions and load types in the target org — connector capabilities and available transformations differ per licence and per connector.

## The authoring boundary still applies

None of these designs can be created over REST. Mapping design, taskflow publish, CDQ rule authoring and scorecard creation are all UI-only walls (see the UI-only walls table). What IS headless: wrapping an existing mapping as a task (`POST /api/v2/mttask`), running it (`POST /api/v2/job`), and monitoring it (`/api/v2/activity/activityLog`). So the split is: design in the canvas, operate by API.

## Why the naming convention is load-bearing, not cosmetic

There is no REST API to read back or diff a mapping's internals, and no version control over the canvas. A written spec with consistent prefixes IS the reviewable artifact and the only practical way to hand a mapping between people. Skipping the convention costs nothing on day one and everything at the first handover.

## Open questions

- Are the expression functions used here (IIF, ISNULL, SYSTIMESTAMP, DATEADD, TO_CHAR/TO_NUMBER, MD5) available across all CDI licence tiers and connectors, or are some gated? Not verified against a live org.
- Whether a CDI sequence generator or a warehouse-side identity column is the better surrogate-key source is a design trade-off this reference does not argue; both appear in the field.
- Snowflake connection body: instanceName display string + connParams field names are NOT captured (only PostgreSQL, MongoDB, JDBCV2 are verified). Recover via CCIManifest.txt + the validator loop.
- Flat-file / on-prem file connection body is NOT captured, incl. how $$SOURCE_DIR maps to a connection vs a mapping parameter, and archive/move-after-read behaviour.
- POST /api/v2/schedule returns 200 but its body (cron/frequency/timezone/start-date) is uncaptured, as is whether a schedule can pass $$LOAD_DATE.
- CDI parameter SETS have no captured endpoint, file format or upload mechanism anywhere in the corpus - only the $$VAR convention is documented.
- Which mapping-task runtime overrides are settable in POST /api/v2/mttask (target load type, truncate flag, pre/post SQL, connection swap) is unknown; one field lesson says source/target retarget is UI-only.
